newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is seen adding reserves to the banking system on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, economists said.
"We're looking for the Fed to inject reserves today with a three-day system RP," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
Saporta said she sees the Fed's daily average add need at $4.5 billion in the remaining three days of the current two-week reserve maintanence period.
Analysts at consulting form MMS International Inc expect the Fed to add reserves via term system RPs on Monday.
Analysts also said a permanent injection of reserves into the system via coupon pass on Monday was possible.

But they added the Fed was more likely to carry a coupon pass on Wednesday, the last day of the current maintenance period. "A coupon pass is possible today, but our best guess for this week is that the Fed will announce the pass on Wednesday for settlement on Thursday," Saporta said.
By 0930 EST/1430 GMT, federal funds were quoted at 5-1/4 percent, in line with the Fed's target for the rate.
